correctness.rationale: For n>=1 and every positive power k, direct induction gives R_h^k(x,g)=(x^{g^{-k}h^k},h^{-k}gh^k). A fixed point requires g to centralize q=h^k and g^k(x)=q(x). In C_{S_n}(q)=product_d(C_d wr S_{m_d}), the containing block has orbit length uniformly distributed in 1..m_d; the net d-rotation is uniform, hence the fixed-point probability is 1/d exactly when ell|k and gcd(d,k/ell)=1. This proves F_h(k)=z(q)B_k(q). Mobius inversion reconstructs all cycles. For n>=3 the trivial center forces h^k=1 if R_h^k=1; letting g range over all S_n forces lcm(1,..,n)|k. The small n=1,2 formulas are individually valid. Direct, independently written permutation enumeration rechecked every h and k=1..12 for n=1..4 and the actual translation cycle profiles.
